paper_1: Train One Sparse Autoencoder Across Multiple Sparsity Budgets to Preserve Interpretability and Accuracy Anonymous ACL submission Abstract Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have proven to be powerful tools for interpreting neural networks by decomposing hidden representations into disentangled, interpretable features via sparsity constraints. However, conventional SAEs are constrained by the fixed sparsity level chosen during training; meeting different sparsity requirements therefore demands separate models and increases the computational footprint during both training and evaluation. We introduce a novel training objective, HierarchicalTopK, which trains a single SAE to optimise reconstructions across multiple sparsity levels simultaneously. Experiments with Gemma-2 2B demonstrate that our approach achieves Pareto-optimal trade-offs between sparsity and explained variance, outperforming traditional SAEs trained at individual sparsity levels. Further analysis shows that HierarchicalTopK preserves high interpretability scores even at higher sparsity. The proposed objective thus closes an important gap between flexibility and interpretability in SAE design. 1 Introduction Transformers have revolutionised natural language processing (NLP) by achieving state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks. Yet their internal representations remain notoriously difficult to interpret, often exhibiting polysemanticity, in which individual neurons activate for semantically unrelated features. To address this challenge, recent work has focused on Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), which learn disentangled, human-interpretable directions in Transformer residual streams by enforcing sparsity constraints on the latent representations. SAEs decompose hidden states into latent embeddings that are theoretically grounded in the independent additivity principle (Ayonrinde et al., 2024). This principle posits that individual features contribute to model behaviour independently, enabling isolated analysis of the latents. In practice, relaxing sparsity constraints (e.g. increasing the number of active latents) often introduces entanglement: latents begin to co-activate for unrelated features, undermining interpretability. Consequently, the effectiveness of existing SAEs is tightly coupled to a single sparsity level fixed during training. We propose HierarchicalTopK, a novel activation mechanism and training objective that enables a single SAE to maintain interpretable features across a range of sparsity levels. Unlike conventional SAEs, which must be retrained to accommodate different sparsity requirements, our method ensures that any subset of latents with k ≤K remains disentangled and faithful to the independent additivity principle. Empirically, HierarchicalTopK SAEs achieve Pareto-optimal trade-offs between sparsity and explained variance, outperforming traditional SAEs trained independently at varying sparsity levels. This work bridges the gap between flexibility and interpretability in SAE design, enabling dynamic adaptation to downstream tasks with varying computational or fidelity requirements. 2 Method Figure 1: Left: SAE trained on a single k. Abstract
001 Tool learning aims to enhance and expand large
002 language models' (LLMs) capabilities with ex003 ternal tools, which has gained significant atten004 tion recently. Current methods have shown that
005 LLMs can effectively handle a certain amount
006 of tools through in-context learning or fine007 tuning. However, in real-world scenarios, the
008 number of tools is typically extensive and ir009 regularly updated, emphasizing the necessity
010 for a dedicated tool retrieval component. Tool
011 retrieval is nontrivial due to the following chal012 lenges: 1) complex user instructions and tool
013 descriptions; 2) misalignment between tool re014 trieval and tool usage models. To address the
015 above issues, we propose to enhance tool re016 trieval with iterative feedback from the large
017 language model. Specifically, we prompt the
018 tool usage model, i.e., the LLM, to provide
019 feedback for the tool retriever model in multi020 round, which could progressively improve the
021 tool retriever's understanding of instructions
022 and tools and reduce the gap between the two
023 standalone components. We build a unified
024 and comprehensive benchmark to evaluate tool
025 retrieval models. The extensive experiments
026 indicate that our proposed approach achieves
027 advanced performance in both in-domain eval028 uation and out-of-domain evaluation.
